source.publication: 2025 Schedule M1R, Age 65 or Older/Disabled Subtraction
source.section: Form M1 lines 1-4, 7-10 (instructions PDF p.13 Standard Deduction Table for Line 4, p.14 Worksheet A, p.39 Tax Rate Schedules, pp.32-38 tax table); Schedule M1R lines 1-13 and Line 10 table (M1R PDF p.1, p.2); Form M1 instructions PDF p.15; M1M PDF p.5 line 16; Schedule M1M line 1 (M1M PDF p.3 'Line 1 - Interest From Municipal Bonds of Another State')

worked: The older spouse is the second person; one qualifying spouse is enough. AGI 20,000 is over both line 10 amounts: the form's for one spouse is 14,500, the projection's 18,000. Federal (given, not tested): federal AGI = IRA distribution 20,000.00 = 20,000.00. Federal taxable income = 20,000.00 - 33,100.00 federal standard deduction (31,500 plus 1 x 1,600) = below zero, so 0.00 (federal senior deduction ignored). Form M1, married filing jointly: line 1 federal AGI 20,000.00. Schedule M1M line 1 other-state municipal interest 40,000.00; line 10 additions 40,000.00; Form M1 line 2 40,000.00; line 3 = 60,000.00. Schedule M1R: line 1 12,000.00; line 2 0.00 (65 or older); line 3 12,000.00; line 4 0.00; line 5 nontaxable Social Security 0.00 - 0.00 = 0.00; line 6 Railroad Retirement Board benefits 0.00; line 7 0.00; line 8 = 12,000.00. Line 9 20,000.00; line 10 14,500.00 (joint, one spouse 65 or older); line 11 5,500.00; line 12 2,750.00; line 13 = 9,250.00. Projection: cap 12,000.00 less benefits received 0.00 and railroad benefits 0.00 = 12,000.00; less 50% x (AGI over 18,000.00) 1,000.00 = 11,000.00, which expected follows; the form gives 9,250.00. Schedule M1M line 40 = Form M1 line 7 subtractions = 0.00 + 11,000.00 + 0.00 + 0.00 = 11,000.00 (lines 12, 16, 17, 25). State income before deduction = 60,000.00 - 11,000.00 = 49,000.00. Standard Deduction Table for Line 4 (PDF p.13): base 29,900.00 plus 1 x 1,550 age box(es) = 31,450.00; AGI is not over 238,950.00, so no Worksheet A. Line 4 = 31,450.00. Form M1 line 8 total = 31,450.00 + 11,000.00 = 42,450.00; line 9 Minnesota taxable income = 60,000.00 - 42,450.00 = 17,550.00. Line 10 tax from the rate schedule (PDF p.39): 5.35% x (17,550.00 - 0.00) = 938.925 = 938.925. The tax table (PDF pp.32-38) gives 939; expected keeps the schedule formula. Line 16 credits 0.00 (the joint-filer Schedule M1C credit is not in the sources and is not applied); state income tax 938.93. Form's own result for comparison: line 9 19,300.00, schedule tax 1,032.55.
accepted_approximations: The age 65 subtraction uses the 18,000 line 10 amount on every joint return; when only one spouse qualifies the amount is 14,500, and no projection field tests both spouses.
Tax comes from the rate schedules at every income; below 86,800 of taxable income the booklet requires its 100-wide tax table.
The Schedule M1C credit for joint filers is not applied because its amount is not in the sources.
